prompt:
Edit image 1. Relight it only: change the time of day, nothing else. Every object keeps exactly its place, size, shape and outline: the same framing, camera and line style, so the result lines up with image 1 pixel for pixel when laid on top of it. Do not move, resize, redraw or remove anything. Objects cut by the edges of image 1 stay cut at exactly the same place.

Image 1 is one piece of a larger painting of a seaside town: wooded hills and houses, a street with parking lots, an amusement park on its boardwalk, the beach and the sea. Relight it in the same light as the rest of the painting.

The new time: early morning, just after sunrise. A soft, fresh light: pale rose and apricot where the low sun from the right touches the tops and the right-facing sides of things, cool lilac-blue in the shade, a faint morning haze over the town. Keep it a storybook painting: the pastel colours stay clean and gentle, a little cooler and paler than midday. The sand is pale peach with a lilac tint, the boardwalk planks soft rose-brown, the white coaster lattice rosy on its sunlit side and lilac on the rest, the street and the parking lots cool grey-lilac.

Every artificial light is switched off.

Where the piece shows the sea, it is a soft pale blue with pink glints on its ripple dashes; hills are misty blue-green and any sky is pale rose-gold.

Shadows stay short and soft, right under each object: no long cast shadows.

Do not add anything new: no people, animals, cars, boats, birds, moon, sun or stars. Do not draw any text, letters, numbers, logos or watermarks.
